scenario.summary: Falcon C2 (aka XG) is a browser-centric threat framework that compromises government web applications to inject malicious JavaScript and install rogue browser extensions. These extensions facilitate credential and email theft while acting as a delivery mechanism for the Antino implant, which establishes persistence on the host and utilizes Microsoft OneDrive as an obfuscated C2 channel.

meta.rationale: Target all corporate and administrative endpoints. Prioritize hosts that access government portals or webmail. Use the lookback period to cover the initial compromise and follow-on C2 phases.
meta.hypothesis: An adversary has established persistence via a malicious browser extension and is using it to communicate with a C2 framework via specific /config/ path structures and POST requests.

hunt.name: Falcon Browser Compromise and Extension Persistence
hunt.description: This hunt identifies the Falcon (XG) browser-based C2 framework by searching for its characteristic /config/ URL patterns and rare POST traffic using Baidu-mimicking tracking markers. When a behavioral match is found, the hunt gates more expensive inventory and file telemetry searches to locate the specific malicious Chrome extension and its core JavaScript components within browser profile directories. This gated approach prioritizes robust behavioral indicators over static extension IDs while ensuring file-level corroboration within the user's extension folder.

config.scoping_notes: Target all corporate and administrative endpoints. Prioritize hosts that access government portals or webmail. Use the lookback period to cover the initial compromise and follow-on C2 phases.
config.beyond_detection: This hunt uses a robust behavioral lead (HTTP /config/ POST patterns) to gate expensive extension inventory and file searches. This correlation between network behavior and file-level extension activity is more resilient than a single rule matching a static extension ID.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, url_hostname, url_path, http_method, url_query, COUNT(*) AS requests, MIN(time) AS first_seen FROM hb_http_activity WHERE (LOWER(url_path) LIKE '/config/%' OR instr(',' || '{{c2_domains}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(url_hostname) || ',') > 0) AND (LOWER(http_method) = 'post' OR LOWER(url_query) LIKE '%hm_lvt_%') AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT device_hostname) <= 5 ORDER BY requests DESC
config.description: Establish a behavioral lead by finding rare POST requests or Baidu-mimicking query parameters directed at /config/ paths or known C2 domains.
config.expected_signal: Rare HTTP POSTs to /config/ paths or query parameters mimicking Baidu analytics. Silence indicates no active framework-style communication was captured during the window.
